subject: Post-call: token economics + batching assumptions (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: token economics + batching assumptions (Nimbus Health)

Hi Laura (and Michael),

Thanks again for the call today — good to hear more about the use cases and SLAs you care about. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a short POC and a ballpark cost model: 

Summary of what I heard from you:
- Primary product: web-based clinician assistant (real-time prompts during charting + patient summarization).
- Expected scale initially: ~5k MAUs, ~3 inference requests/user/day (mix of short queries + one longer summary).
- Typical lengths: inputs ~120 tokens, outputs ~650 tokens (average).
- Traffic profile: diurnal web traffic with spikes during morning rounds; potential nightly bulk summarization batch for archived notes (~500k tokens/night).
- Latency target: 95% under 1s for interactive flows.

Open items for cost/technical qualification:
1) Monthly token volume: with the numbers above we estimate ~5k*3*(120+650) ≈ 11.55M tokens/month. Can you confirm if that sounds right for your early launch (or share a target range)?
2) Budget range: do you have a committed monthly spend or target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for? You mentioned keeping inferencing costs predictable — a ballpark range helps us optimize model choice and batching.
3) Concurrency & batching expectations: Are interactive requests strictly single-shot per user (no multi-turn streaming), or do you expect multi-turn sessions where KV cache reuse would reduce tokens? Also, what peak concurrent requests should we size for (estimate)?
4) Nightly bulk: confirm if the nightly summarization can accept higher latency (minutes) and be routed to cheaper batch nodes.

Attached is a first-pass estimate (redwood_estimate_nimbus_v1.pdf) and a tiny traffic template (nimbus_sample_traffic_template.csv) — if you can drop a week of timestamped request counts into that template we’ll run a brief cost simulation and propose a recommended config (batch window, concurrency per GPU, and suggestion on quantization / model variant).

Proposed next steps:
- Laura: share a 7-day sample traffic CSV (timestamps + request type) if possible by EOD Thursday.
- Redwood: run token-level cost simulation and return a 2-page POC plan + estimated $/1M tokens and projected monthly bill.
- Agree on a short POC timeframe (2–3 weeks).

If the budget range is tight we can prioritize a smaller model + aggressive quantization and a batching-first config. If you want maximum quality we’ll show the tradeoffs with projected unit economics.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood_estimate_nimbus_v1.pdf (PDF, 42KB); nimbus_sample_traffic_template.csv (CSV, 2KB)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: token economics + batching assumptions (Nimbus Health)

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Token volumes: the 11–12M tokens/month ballpark seems plausible for the initial launch. If adoption is faster, we could see 20–25M/month in 3–6 months.
- Budget: we’re targeting an initial budget of $5k–$8k/month for inference (hosted + infra). For procurement we’d need a predictable unit price to model scenarios — ideally we’d like to see a target cost per 1M tokens in your estimate.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent interactive requests across our region ~25–35 (peak morning window). Requests are mostly single-shot but some flows do 2–3 quick follow-ups (so KV reuse likely minimal today).
- Nightly batch: yes — nightly summarization can tolerate higher latency and be scheduled on cheaper capacity. That workload is ~400–600k tokens/night initially.

We’ll try to get you a week of traffic into your CSV by Friday. If you could include a pricing sketch that shows tradeoffs (batching window vs latency vs $/1M tokens) that’d be super helpful.

Laura
VP Product, Nimbus Health
laura.chen@nimbushealth.com

On Tue, May 12, 2026 at 3:08 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:

To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: token economics + batching assumptions (Nimbus Health)

Karthik — quick internal notes for the POC we should include in the estimate: 

- Assumptions to surface explicitly in the doc: average output length 650 tokens, 3 requests/user/day, 7-day active look.
- Batching config options to model: 1) low-latency: 10ms batch window, target concurrency per GPU 48, modest cache reuse; 2) cost-optimized: 50–100ms window with continuous batching and KV cache disabled for simplicity (but we should note multi-turn affects this).
- Suggest we present three cost points in the PDF: conservative (higher quality model, no quantization), balanced (4-bit quantization suggestion with fallback), and aggressive-cost (int8 quant + bigger batching windows).
- Note: include ops note on warm KV cache savings assumption — show delta if 20% of requests hit the cache.

I’ll help with the latency/cost table. Send me the traffic CSV when Laura provides it and I’ll run the sim.

—Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: token economics + batching assumptions (Nimbus Health)

Laura — thanks for the quick clarifications, and that budget range is helpful. A few concrete next actions from our side: 

1) Redwood will run two simulated cost profiles once we receive your 7-day CSV: 
   - Profile A (balanced): assumes 10ms batch window, continuous batching with target per-GPU concurrency 48, and 4-bit quantization where feasible.
   - Profile B (cost-optimized): assumes 50ms batch window, larger continuous batching, int8 quant option, and routes nightly batch to low-cost pool.

2) We’ll include an explicit $/1M tokens line for both profiles and a sensitivity table that shows how unit cost moves with monthly volume (5M / 12M / 25M tokens).

3) For the POC we’d like a small token-level run: if you can provide the sample CSV we’ll run an internal simulation and share results in ~48 hours. With your permission we may also run a short controlled workload on Hosted Redwood to validate latency vs batch-window tradeoffs (no production data needed).

Could you confirm: are you comfortable with Redwood running the simulation on the CSV (we treat it as non-sensitive) and do you want us to include worst-case 99th percentile latency projections in the doc?

Once we have your CSV we’ll send a 2-page POC plan + the two cost profiles.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_estimate_nimbus_v1.pdf (resent)
